newsitem.title: USA: Thousands of mink die after raid on Oregon farm.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of mink die after raid on Oregon farm.

text.p: More than 2,400 mink were confirmed dead on Monday after fences at an Oregon ranch were cut and the animals' cages opened, officials said.

The ranch near Mount Angel, about 30 miles (50 km) south of Portland, had about 9,000 mink, mostly babies less than 6 weeks old. A team of vandals cut a perimeter fence in "about a dozen places" early on Friday, said Marion County Sheriff's Sgt. Bob Stai.
The suspects then went through the farm systematically opening small cagelike structures that each contained a mother mink and a litter of tiny kits less than 6 inches (15 cm) long.
The baby mink are helpless without their mothers and many of them died when the mink scattered after the cages were opened, officials said. Some 400 mothers died, many from exposure.
There were no suspects in the incident, but the FBI is investigating the case as a possible violation of the Animal Enterprise Terrorism Act, said FBI spokesman Pat Geonetta.

Marsha Kelly of Fur Commission U.S.A., which represents the nation's 1,000 mink farms, said the farm had 1,600 breeding female mink and between 6,000 and 8,000 kits, who at that age are completely dependent on their mothers for warmth and food.
"You would think they would wait until the babies were weaned and had a chance for survival," said Stai of the sheriff's department.
Farmer Rick Arritola estimated the death toll would rise to 5,000 mink and his loss is estimated to total several hundred thousand dollars, Kelly said.
She said incidents of vandalism to fur farms have been increasing in recent years, with about 25 recorded in the past 18 months alone.
